claims.text: Black-grass is recorded here as Alopecurus myosuroides, in the family Poaceae.
The dataset treats Black-grass as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Black-grass is an annual tufted grass. Young leaves are fine and smooth; older flowering plants bear narrow, dark-purplish heads.
Young black-grass can resemble loose silky-bent; a purple or reddish leaf sheath alone is insufficient to distinguish them.
AHDB's UK arable guidance combines rotation changes, suitable spring cropping, competitive crops and delayed autumn sowing to reduce black-grass pressure. Timing must be adapted locally.
AHDB describes rotational inversion tillage and hand-roguing low-density patches as parts of black-grass control. Prevent surviving plants returning seed.
Use several complementary measures and reduce seed movement on machinery or infested material; non-chemical measures also help protect herbicide efficacy.

claims.text: Charlock is recorded here as Sinapis arvensis, in the family Brassicaceae.
The dataset treats Charlock as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Charlock is a hairy annual broadleaf with irregularly toothed leaves and pale-yellow flowers with four petals.
AHDB reports competition with winter wheat and winter oilseed rape in the UK. Control is particularly difficult in brassica crops; this is not a Pakistani treatment recommendation.

claims.text: Cleavers is recorded here as Galium aparine, in the family Rubiaceae.
The dataset treats Cleavers as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Cleavers has scrambling stems, whorled leaves and hooked bristles that cling to clothing and other plants. Tiny white flowers later form bristly fruits.
Cleavers is an annual; the Danish crop-protection guide describes both summer- and winter-annual growth.
In garden beds, remove rooted cleavers plants or hoe young seedlings before flowering and seed production. Minimize unnecessary soil disturbance.
RHS garden guidance includes mulching bare soil to suppress new cleavers seedlings. Recheck boundaries and young plantings for new growth.
The Danish crop guide reports that cleavers can contribute to lodging and crop losses; the significance depends on crop and infestation.

species.expert_review_status: Not independently reviewed by a local botanist/agronomist

claims.text: Common chickweed is recorded here as Stellaria media, in the family Caryophyllaceae.
The dataset treats Common chickweed as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Common chickweed forms low, fragile stems with opposite, pointed oval leaves. Its white petals are deeply notched; mouseear chickweed has more densely hairy leaves.
Iowa State describes common chickweed as a winter or summer annual.
Pull shallow-rooted plants or hoe seedlings on a dry day before they set seed. Keep flowering material out of ordinary home compost where seed may survive.
For garden beds, mulch or suitable ground cover can suppress new chickweed seedlings. Avoid unnecessary soil disturbance that brings buried seed to the surface.

claims.text: Common wheat is recorded here as Triticum aestivum, in the family Poaceae.
The dataset treats Common wheat as a crop class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Common wheat is an annual cereal grass cultivated for grain, forage or cover cropping; its leaves are linear.
NC State describes wheat as a cover crop that can suppress weeds. This does not authorize removing a desired wheat crop or selecting a herbicide for it.

claims.text: Fat hen is recorded here as Chenopodium album, in the family Amaranthaceae.
The dataset treats Fat hen as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Fat hen is an erect annual herb with elliptic to diamond-shaped, toothed leaves and a pale mealy lower surface. Flowers occur in dense small green clusters.
AWRI describes competition for water and nutrients in its viticulture context; regional crop relevance requires separate verification.
AWRI describes mowing before flowering to reduce seed set and hand-pulling before seeding. This information comes from Australian vineyard management.
Monitor new growth after rain or irrigation and prevent seed production; the source describes rapid growth in moist conditions and long-lived buried seed.

claims.text: Loose silky-bent is recorded here as Apera spica-venti, in the family Poaceae.
The dataset treats Loose silky-bent as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Loose silky-bent is an annual grass with smooth leaf sheaths and an open, feathery flowerhead. It can resemble young black-grass.
AHDB reports that grass breaks or spring cropping can reduce loose silky-bent populations in UK cereal rotations.
In reduced-tillage settings, AHDB describes allowing emergence before cultivating or harrowing seedlings when soil is dry.
Resistance to ALS inhibitors is reported in parts of mainland Europe. ALS inhibitors are HRAC Group 2; this information does not establish local resistance or efficacy.

claims.text: Maize is recorded here as Zea mays, in the family Poaceae.
The dataset treats Maize as a crop class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Maize, also called corn, is an annual grass crop in Poaceae. It is wind-pollinated and cultivated for its grain and other crop uses.
NC State's garden guidance favors mulch around established corn rather than cultivation that may injure its roots. Do not interpret a maize prediction as a weed-removal instruction.

claims.text: Scentless mayweed is recorded here as Tripleurospermum inodorum, in the family Asteraceae.
The dataset treats Scentless mayweed as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Scentless mayweed has finely divided, thread-like leaves and white daisy-like flowerheads with yellow centers. Non-flowering mayweeds can be difficult to distinguish.
Regional guides describe annual to short-lived perennial behavior. A growth-stage photograph alone does not establish the full life cycle.
Washington State guidance supports hand-pulling small infestations. Mowing can slow flowering, but plants may flower again below the cut height.
Competitive vegetation can suppress scentless mayweed, and cleaning equipment helps limit movement into new areas.
AHDB reports UK populations resistant to ALS inhibitors. These are HRAC Group 2. Resistance testing and local professional advice are needed before a control programme is chosen.

claims.text: Shepherd's purse is recorded here as Capsella bursa-pastoris, in the family Brassicaceae.
The dataset treats Shepherd's purse as a weed class. This project label does not decide whether a plant is unwanted in your field.
Shepherd's purse forms a basal leaf rosette; flowering stems bear distinctive triangular or heart-shaped seed pods. Older rosette leaves can be deeply lobed.
Iowa State describes a winter annual; Washington State notes annual, winter-annual and occasional biennial behavior.

general.text: Integrated weed management combines identification, site assessment, competitive planting, soil-cover methods and timely weed removal. Tactics depend on the planting system; landscape guidance is not a crop-specific field prescription.
In landscape beds, competitive plants and suitable mulches reduce exposed soil and suppress new weeds. The UC source recommends maintaining coverage and monitoring new emergence.
General landscape guidance includes removing young weeds before seed production and shallow hoeing for annual weeds, while protecting desirable plants and limiting unnecessary disturbance.

HRAC Group 1 denotes inhibition of ACCase; Group 2 denotes inhibition of ALS. These are mode-of-action classifications, not proof that a product will control a particular population or be safe in a crop.
A weed is a plant growing where it is unwanted. Crop-versus-weed labels in the classifier describe the dataset classes; whether to retain or remove a plant depends on its context.
